author: GamingBolt
description:
Presentation-wise, Where the Seeds Fall doesn't look too shabby, even if the character models and animation might convince you otherwise. Aside from some iffy lighting, the minimalist art direction, combined with the watercolor backdrops, is easy on the eyes. A scene where the nameless lays out the plot and his own past against a stunning sunset would have been better if the clouds had improved aliasing, but I digress. As for the music, I struggle to recall anything noteworthy.

Ten bucks is ten bucks, though, and for some, that's enough. Its setting and overall premise are acceptable enough on their own, but compared to so many other top-notch 3D platformers, speed-run-focused or otherwise? Not quite. Where the Seeds Fall is a notable effort from CygamesEdge. I only hope their next effort either uses its runtime to tell a more entertaining self-contained story with better movement. title: Where The Seeds Fall PS5 Review - Is $10 Low Enough?

author: GamingBolt
description:
Ashes of the Singularity 2 might look like a chaotic game that only fans of the genre might enjoy. However, its generally slow pace of gameplay and emphasis on long-term plans and unit compositions over micro-management lends itself quite well to newer players as well. 

This paired with a fun campaign with an interesting story, as well as plenty of gameplay variety offered in Skirmish and multiplayer modes makes Ashes of Singularity 2 feel like a complete package.
title: Ashes of the Singularity 2 Review: Is This As Big As RTS Gets?

author: GamingBolt
description:
When it comes to your average day-to-day needs, everyone likely has the same concern, especially about the necessities. When it comes to Grand Theft Auto 6, I'm willing to bet you never thought we'd hear the words “almost one week away from launch.” Or that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, instead of reiterating that there wouldn't be any more delays, stated that development is now complete. But here we are, and there is Rockstar Games' most ambitious, most realistic, and arguably its most life-devouring game to date.

And yet, against all odds, the development team had more to share over the past several days. Pre-loads are now live, so now is a good time to clear out the 212 GB of space required. Oh, and the game targets 30 frames per second on all consoles. Yes, even the PS5 Pro.
title: GTA 6 Could Be PS5 Pro’s Biggest System Seller Yet, Specs Revealed
